2607.20995.title: Where Animacy Lives in Large Language Models: Tracing the Circuits of the Animacy Concept
2607.20995.paper_summary: Distinguishing animate from inanimate concepts in written language requires more than shallow text processing, as it involves recognizing complex selectional constraints and contextual cues, such as verb-argument interactions. Yet, current large language models (LLMs) appear to be capable of doing it. We investigate whether this animacy-sensitive behavior of LLMs can be traced to a localized set of causally relevant components and connections. To do so, we construct a controlled dataset of minimal pairs and perform circuit discovery on four open-weight models. Through in-depth experiments and ablations, we show that a causal mechanism responsible for handling animacy in these models does exist, thus discovering an animacy circuit. At the same time, this circuit appears to be less localized compared to other known ones and generalizes only partially across models and animacy tasks, confirming the distributed, context-dependent, and somewhat graded nature of the animacy concept.
2607.20995.paper_summary_zh: 區分書面語言中的有生命與無生命概念需要的不僅僅是淺層的文本處理，因為這涉及到識別複雜的選擇約束和上下文線索，例如動詞-論元互動。 然而，目前的大型語言模型（LLMs）似乎能夠做到這一點。 我們研究這些 LLMs 的有生命感知行為是否可以追溯到一組局部的因果相關組件和連結。 為此，我們構建了一個最小對的受控數據集，並對四個開放權重模型進行電路發現。 通過深入的實驗和消融，我們顯示出一種負責處理這些模型中有生命感的因果機制確實存在，從而發現了一個有生命電路。 同時，這個電路似乎與其他已知電路相比不那麼局部，並且在模型和有生命任務之間僅部分泛化，確認了有生命概念的分佈性、上下文依賴性和某種程度的漸進性質。
